evals.prompt: Add rate limiting: at most 10 requests per minute per client across the whole API, and a stricter limit of 3 requests per minute on POST /auth/login (just return { ok: true } from it for now).
evals.expected_output: @nestjs/throttler with a global ThrottlerGuard (APP_GUARD) and @Throttle override on the login route.
assertions: The 4th POST /auth/login within a minute returns 429
The 11th GET / within a minute returns 429 while the first 10 succeed

evals.prompt: Add standard security headers to every response, and enable CORS so that only https://app.example.com can call the API from a browser, with credentials allowed.
evals.expected_output: Built-in app.useSecurityHeaders() (NestJS 12.1+, Helmet 8 defaults, no extra package) or helmet(); app.enableCors({ origin: 'https://app.example.com', credentials: true }).
assertions: Responses carry standard security headers (x-content-type-options: nosniff)
A preflight from https://app.example.com is allowed with credentials
A preflight from another origin does not get that origin allowed
[docs] Uses the built-in app.useSecurityHeaders() (NestJS 12.1+) instead of adding helmet

evals.prompt: POST /users stores the raw password in passwordHash. Hash passwords properly before storing, and add POST /auth/login { email, password } that returns { ok: true } for correct credentials and 401 otherwise.
evals.expected_output: Passwords hashed with a slow, salted algorithm (the docs recommend PasswordHasher from @nestjs/authentication, scrypt; argon2/bcrypt acceptable); login verifies with the hasher.
assertions: Login with the correct password returns { ok: true }
Login with a wrong password returns 401
The stored password is not the plaintext
Uses a password-hashing algorithm (scrypt/argon2/bcrypt), not a plain digest such as sha256/md5
